summary: Radar for 2026-10-17, GLP-1 focus. Three stories are new and checked this run. (1) On Oct 14 the MHRA and West Midlands Police seized more than 12,000 fake retatrutide and tirzepatide pens worth about £2m. That fits our best lane, calm warnings about gray-market products, and a new Penn analysis of Reddit posts about unregulated retatrutide adds to it. (2) On Oct 15 the EMA's CHMP recommended orforglipron (Foundayo) for obesity and type 2 diabetes. The European Commission decision is still pending. This is a named next-gen pill, the format that works in both Shorts and long-form. (3) An exploratory SURPASS-CVOT analysis (Eur J Prev Cardiol, Oct 15) looked at people with type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular disease and a history of heart failure. Death or a heart-failure event happened in 18.2% on tirzepatide vs 21.5% on dulaglutide. It's a plain 'Can tirzepatide…?' question with a named drug. Evergreen tirzepatide lanes still score high: muscle and strength training, and the SURMOUNT-5 side-effect head-to-head. The NAION vision-loss study (Annals of Internal Medicine, about 3–4 extra cases per 10,000 over 18 months) is peaking. Scare topics about approved drugs do poorly for us, so it's ranked lower and needs a numbers-first, calm angle. Checks that changed the picture: the 'FDA adds new warning to Wegovy' items are SEO spam pages, and the only related FDA label action found is from January 2026 (the FDA asked for suicide warnings to be removed), so they're excluded. The semaglutide asthma/COPD data is an ERS conference result from September, now being recirculated. Rejected: price-shopping or compounded-cost content, and anything that could serve as a GLP-1 misuse guide for people with eating disorders.

candidates.topic: Fake tirzepatide and 'retatrutide' pens: the UK seized more than 12,000 counterfeit pens worth about £2m in Birmingham (MHRA and West Midlands Police, Oct 14, 2026)
candidates.angle: A calm 'what's confirmed vs not' decoder. Confirmed: the MHRA says the seized pens weren't assessed for safety or quality, and there's no guarantee what's in them. Retatrutide isn't authorised in the UK and is investigational in the US as of Oct 2026. Close on the safe route: a prescriber and a registered pharmacy. Never name sellers or say how to buy.
candidates.why_now: An official UK seizure 3 days ago that names both tirzepatide and retatrutide. It follows the bootleg 'Reta' death reports to the FDA (our best Short, 165 views) and lots of 'retatrutide approval status' searches. UK readers are a core part of our audience.

evidence.signal: Oct 14 raid: more than 12,000 fake retatrutide and tirzepatide pens, plus packaging for about 30,000 more
Mainstream coverage of the retatrutide black market (Oct 14)

candidates.topic: Orforglipron (Foundayo) recommended for EU approval: the CHMP adopted a positive opinion on Oct 15, 2026, for weight management and type 2 diabetes. The Commission decision is pending
candidates.angle: 'Lilly's GLP-1 pill just cleared a big step in Europe: what's different about it?' It's a non-peptide pill that can be taken at any time of day, with no food or water rules (unlike the semaglutide pill). In the EMA's summary, adults with obesity or overweight lost about 5–11% of body weight at 72 weeks, depending on dose, vs about 2–2.5% on placebo. It's already FDA-approved for weight management in the US (April 2026). Wording must say 'recommended', not 'approved', in the EU.
candidates.why_now: The CHMP opinion came 2 days ago and is being covered by finance and pharma press. Consumer creators haven't covered it much yet, and Medscape just published 'What to Know About the GLP-1 Pill Orforglipron'. Named next-gen drugs are our only long-forms that get views.

evidence.signal: EMA panel backs Foundayo for obesity and type 2 diabetes
Positive opinion on 15 Oct 2026; second oral GLP-1 in the EU after the Wegovy pill
FDA approved orforglipron for chronic weight management (April 2026)

candidates.topic: Can tirzepatide help people with diabetes and heart failure? SURPASS-CVOT exploratory analysis: death or a heart-failure event in 18.2% on tirzepatide vs 21.5% on dulaglutide (HR 0.83)
candidates.angle: A plain question answered by about 10 s. Population: adults with type 2 diabetes, atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and a history of heart failure (about 20% of 13,299 participants), followed for about 4 years. It's exploratory, so say 'linked to' and treat it as hypothesis-generating. Name both drugs, with tirzepatide first. Mention common stomach side effects.
candidates.why_now: Published Oct 15 (Eur J Prev Cardiol, covered by AJMC). It extends our tirzepatide heart-failure Short (52 Instagram reach) with a cleaner, single-number title. Hardly any creators have covered it.

evidence.signal: 18.2% vs 21.5%, HR 0.83 (95% CI 0.70–0.99) in patients with heart failure
Meta-analysis of tirzepatide's effects on heart biomarkers and exercise capacity in heart failure (Oct 13)

candidates.angle: 'Losing weight on tirzepatide? 3 ways to protect your muscle': a direct 'you' hook, a named drug and a numbered promise, the formula behind our 130-view Short. Exercise tips say start gently; protein tips say check first if you have kidney disease.

candidates.angle: A follow-up to our 109-view head-to-head. Name both drugs, give the answer by about 10 s, put each drug's name next to its number, and add practical tips for easing nausea and constipation (fluids 'unless you've been told to limit fluids').

candidates.topic: Unregulated 'retatrutide' on Reddit vs the real trial: Penn's AI analysis of 13,589 self-reported users found increased appetite was the most-reported symptom, then fatigue (15.2%) and nausea (11.6%)
candidates.angle: 'Why a research peptide isn't the trial drug.' The Phase 2 trial's side effects were mostly stomach-related, while Reddit users most often reported increased appetite, fatigue, insomnia and a faster heart rate. That's one sign the vials may not contain what the label says. Present it as self-reported and unverified. Use 'most-reported' wording, check whether the study is peer-reviewed or still a preprint, and point people to a prescriber.
candidates.why_now: Penn's release (Oct 15) has been picked up by Medscape ('Unexpected Retatrutide Side Effects Reported by Reddit Users') and Health and Me. Searches for 'retatrutide side effects' are high right after the bootleg-death story.

evidence.signal: AI surfaces unreported GLP-1 side effects in Reddit posts
Underlying study (check whether it's peer-reviewed yet)

candidates.topic: Why some people lose 20% on semaglutide or tirzepatide and others lose much less: the spread of results in the STEP and SURMOUNT trials
candidates.angle: 'Lost less on tirzepatide than your friend? Here's what the trials show': each trial's average plus how far individual results spread, the factors linked to a smaller response (for example type 2 diabetes), and why an average isn't a promise. Encouraging, with no dosing talk; suggest talking to the prescriber.

candidates.topic: Semaglutide pill vs orforglipron pill: how the two GLP-1 pills differ (peptide vs non-peptide, food and water rules, trial results) as of Oct 2026
candidates.angle: A plain-language Short, our proven format for pills (55 YouTube views, 52 Instagram reach). The semaglutide pill (approved Dec 22, 2025) has to be taken on an empty stomach with a little water; orforglipron has no food or water rules. Name both drugs. Don't declare a winner without a direct trial, and include 'don't change your current medicines on your own'.
candidates.why_now: Fierce Pharma's oral GLP-1 tracker (Oct 17) and the EU recommendation for orforglipron. There's also a new qualitative study from the Phase 3 orforglipron-vs-oral-semaglutide trial (Patient, Oct 16).

candidates.topic: Where compounded semaglutide and tirzepatide ingredients come from: FDA inspectors reported black mold and insects at Chinese plants supplying them (Bloomberg, Oct 15), and both firms were placed on an FDA import alert
candidates.angle: 'What's confirmed vs not' about compounded GLP-1s. Quote the FDA inspection findings, give the import-alert dates and point out that compounded versions aren't FDA-approved or reviewed for safety. Calm, attributed, no fear-bait, no seller names, and it ends on approved medicines through a prescriber. Add 'don't stop or change your current medicines on your own'.

Scare topics have done poorly for us, so lead with the reassuring absolute risk.
